Jeffries is set to become one of Trump’s most prominent opponents for final two years of his presidency
Democrats on Wednesday resoundingly nominated Hakeem Jeffries to serve as speaker of the House when the new Congress begins next year, teeing him up to become the first Black lawmaker to lead the chamber.
A New York congressman who has served as the Democratic minority leader since 2023, Jeffries is set to become one of Donald Trump’s most prominent opponents for the final two years of his presidency, when Democrats will control both the Senate and House of Representatives and are expected to undertake aggressive efforts to check his powers.
Democrats nominated Jeffries despite concerns from some progressives that he represents a politically risky status quo for a party that is looking to capitalize on a surprisingly good performance in the midterms, where voters swept them back into power in both the House and Senate with significant majorities.
The vote took place at a caucus meeting held behind closed doors, and no other lawmaker challenged Jeffries for the speakership nomination. A source familiar with the tally said Jeffries was supported by 251 of 262 ballots cast.
Following the election, Jeffries posted a photo of himself as a child on X , and wrote: “Thank you House Democrats. Together, we will deliver bold change. And make a big difference in the lives of the American people!”
The 56-year-old is set to be formally elected speaker when the House of Representatives convenes at the beginning of next year, with Democrats controlling their largest majority in nearly two decades. He would become the first Democratic House speaker since Nancy Pelosi, who will retire from Congress at the end of this year.
The caucus additionally elected the California congressman Ted Lieu to serve as their chair, the first Asian American to hold that position. Fellow Californian Pete Aguilar was named the incoming majority whip, and will be the first Latino in that role.
In office since 2013, Jeffries served as House Democratic caucus chair during Pelosi’s second stint as speaker, from 2019 to 2023. He took over as leader when she stepped down after Democrats lost their House majority in 2022, but rankled progressives by refusing to endorse proposals to create a Medicare for All healthcare system, and for not taking a strong stance against aid to Israel amid accusations it carried out a genocide in Gaza. Earlier this month, Indivisible, a nationwide progressive organizing group, released a poll that found only 28% of registered voters view Jeffries favorably.
He has recently sought to bridge those divides, and on Tuesday announced his support for lowering the age of eligibility for Medicare, and expanding its coverage to include vision and dental treatments, and to offer it to children. He has also called for “dramatic change” in the US relationship with Israel, though in July did not vote for an amendment that would have cut military aid to the Middle Eastern ally.
The speaker of the House is one of the most powerful figures in Congress, and has the power to decide which bills come to the floor of the lower chamber. Should Jeffries win election, he will be tasked with balancing the demands of an ideologically diverse caucus composed of liberals and centrists, as well as lawmakers from safe blue districts and others from areas that Trump won handily in the 2024 vote.
The leaders of the Congressional Progressive caucus cheered Jeffries’ nomination, while noting they expected him to collaborate on passing their preferred healthcare and immigration priorities.
“CPC leadership is working daily with Leader Jeffries to make sure the Democratic majority delivers on our mandate for bold change,” its chair, Greg Casar, and his top deputies said.
“We have made significant progress since the election to lay out a progressive agenda alongside leader Jeffries, and the CPC will work with him to pass the first year of Medicare For All, an end to for-profit immigrant detention centers, and so much more.”
Some newly elected Democrats said they had opted to oppose Jeffries, because they were not convinced he would champion their priorities as speaker,
Don Leonard, a newly elected Democrat representing an Ohio district Trump won two years ago, told CNN he would not vote for Jeffries unless he won commitments to end aid to Israel, and undo the supreme court’s Citizens United ruling, which allowed outside groups to spend unlimited amounts on elections.
Seven newly elected progressive Democrats – Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez of New York, Adam Hamawy of New Jersey, Frederick Haynes of Texas, Melat Kiros of Colorado, Donavan McKinney of Michigan and Chris Rabb of Pennsylvania – announced after the vote that they had also opposed making Jeffries speaker, at least for now.
“Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues. We have worked to secure commitments from leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations,” the lawmakers said.
“While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of leadership. Those conversations are ongoing. As such, our vote in caucus today was no.”
Over in the Senate, the party’s leader, Chuck Schumer, is facing a challenge from Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead the party next year, when Democrats will take control of the chamber after winning 56 seats in the midterms. That contest is set to be decided at a caucus vote scheduled for 1 December.

Democrats in the US House of Representatives officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber.
The House will elect its new Speaker on 3 January, when the next term begins and Democrats will be in the majority.
His election to the powerful position - the Speaker is in line to succeed the president after the vice-president - is widely expected. Should he win, Jeffries will preside over his party's largest House majority in years and benefit from the partnership with a Senate also under Democrats' control.
Jeffries told reporters after the vote that the nomination was "a high honour and a distinct privilege".
As of Wednesday, Democrats will hold at least 257 seats in the House next year, with seven races still uncalled, which is well beyond the 218 needed for a majority.

Mary Peltola defeated the state's Republican incumbent after a controversial race
Democrat Mary Peltola has won Alaska's hard-fought Senate race, completing a sweeping victory for the party in the US upper house in the midterm elections.
The win gives the Democrats a 56th Senate seat following a tumultuous and controversial election in Alaska, which featured alleged spoiler recruitment efforts and unprecedented court battles.
It took two full weeks of counting to call a winner in the 3 November poll due to the logistical challenge of collecting ballots from across the state's remote expanse.
It is the ninth Senate seat the Democrats have taken from Republicans in the midterms, giving the party control of the US Congress for the last two years of Donald Trump's presidency.
The Democrats also won back the House of Representatives, the lower chamber.
Peltola defeated the incumbent Republican senator, Dan S Sullivan, who is yet to comment.
In her victory statement, Peltola said the "status quo in DC is not working for Alaska".
She recalled speaking to "elders in tears about empty fish racks" and to parents in rural Alaska choosing between heating their homes and putting food on the table.
Peltola is the first Alaska Native elected to the US Senate, and is the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat in Alaska since 2008.
Donald Trump won the state by 13 points in the 2024 presidential election, but defeat for the Republicans in this year's US Senate race in the state caps off a string of losses in the midterms for the president's party.
Many voters across the United States cited cost-of-living issues as a factor that affected how they cast their ballots.
Trump says Alaska voters chose the wrong Dan Sullivan. What does the data show?
Could Alaska's fishing industry tilt Washington's balance of power?
Peltola's campaign had come under fire after the New York Times , external reported that her team worked with people who tried to recruit so-called spoiler candidates in an alleged attempt to confuse voters.
The alleged scheme led to a candidate named Daniel J Sullivan - a complete political unknown residing in a small coastal town who shared a name with the state's current US Senator and incumbent, Dan S Sullivan - contesting the race.
After legal challenges, state courts ruled that Daniel J Sullivan could remain on the ballot, and election officials distinguished them on election materials.
Peltola denied having knowledge of the alleged plot but her campaign swiftly came under fire, and both the US justice department and Alaska's Republican governor said they would launch investigations.
The Trump administration also filed a lawsuit attempting to stop the certification of the election results if the incumbent Republican Senator Sullivan lost.
A federal judge, though, dismissed the case, following legal challenges from Alaska election officials as well as the Peltola campaign and voting groups.
Due to Alaska's ranked-choice voting system, voters confused about which Dan Sullivan was the incumbent could have simply chosen both men, listing them as their first and second choices.
If they did so, after the first round of voting was complete, tabulation would have re-allocated any votes from Daniel J Sullivan - who stood little to no chance of winning - to Dan S Sullivan.
Experts told the BBC that this process made it difficult for any potential spoiler candidate to have any impact on the results.
An analysis by BBC Verify found that even if every vote for Daniel J Sullivan had gone to the incumbent, Dan S Sullivan, Peltola would still have won.
The Democratic win in Alaska cements the party's majority in the US Senate, as the party now has 56 seats to the Republicans' 44.
The most senior Democrat in the Senate, Chuck Schumer, said Peltola had run "a pitch-perfect campaign devoted to the issues Alaskans care most about". Hailing the Democrats' final tally in the Senate, he said: "56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago."
The Alaska seat was initially one of several toss-up races that appeared as a must-win for Democrats if they wanted to gain control of the US Senate. But by the time Peltola was called the winner, they had seats to spare.
With 99% of ballots counted, Peltola had slightly more than 50% of the votes, while Sullivan trailed on less than 46%.
Sullivan, a former Alaska attorney general and an ally of Trump, campaigned on his record of delivering energy and military investment for the state.
Peltola promised Alaskans a more independent voice in Washington.
"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," she said in her victory statement.
"I will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in DC and deliver results for Alaska's working families."

The New York congressman is nominated after Democrats gained control of Congress in this month’s midterm elections.
Washington, DC, United States – Hakeem Jeffries has become the first Black lawmaker officially nominated for speaker of the US House of Representatives, marking a milestone in the country’s political history.
In a closed-door vote on Wednesday, the 56-year-old New York congressman secured his party’s nomination for the post just weeks after Democrats scored sweeping victories in the midterm elections, reclaiming control of both chambers of the US Congress.
After voting concluded, Jeffries took to social media to thank his fellow Democrats for their support.
“Together, we will deliver bold change. And make a big difference in the lives of the American people!” he wrote in a post on X.
Amid growing dissent among progressives over his leadership, Jeffries confirmed plans to force members of his party to take a recorded vote on Wednesday.
Some of those members, most of whom were elected this month, declined to say whether they would support Jeffries. Several said they wanted a leader who would support bold, populist policies they had campaigned on.
One of the most vocal holdouts, Congressman-elect Don Leonard of Ohio, refused to commit to Jeffries unless he received guarantees on some progressive priorities, including halting US military aid to Israel and reforming campaign finance standards set by the Supreme Court case Citizens United.
“Unless Speaker Jeffries is willing to commit to enforcing our nation’s laws like the Leahy Law against Israeli genocide in Gaza, unless the speaker is willing to get to the heart of this crisis, which is Citizens United, he will not have my vote,” the Ohio Democrat said in a video posted to social media.
Jeffries has received pushback within some Democratic circles over his record on Israel and ties to pro-Israel lobbying groups, like AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee. During an interview with The Atlantic magazine on Tuesday, Jeffries addressed some of that criticism, calling for “dramatic change” in the Middle East and a two-state solution.
Despite some opposition in Wednesday’s vote, Jeffries received overwhelming support from the House Democratic Caucus with 251 members voting to back his candidacy. Only 11 members opposed it.
Seven of those who voted against Jeffries included newly-elected Democrats Darializa Avila Chevalier of New York, Adam Hamawy of New Jersey, Frederick Haynes of Texas, Melat Kiros of Colorado, Donavan McKinney of Michigan, Chris Rabb of Pennsylvania and Claire Valdez of New York.
Those members released a statement, which was shared with Al Jazeera, detailing their opposition they said was over failure to receive commitments from Jeffries on policies like “Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics or ending the genocide in Gaza”.
“While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of leadership”, the soon-to-be lawmakers wrote. “Those conversations are ongoing. As such, our vote in caucus today was no”.
Most Democrats, however, praised Jeffries’ nomination for speaker, which will put him on track to become one of Donald Trump’s top political opponents during the final two years of his presidency.
Outgoing Congresswoman Nancy Pelosi, who served for eight years as the first female speaker during two non-consecutive terms, marked the historic moment with a social media post, which included a photo of her holding Jeffries hand.
“Congratulations, Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries!” she wrote.
Just before the vote, Jeffries took to social media to post a Bible verse from the book of Corinthians reading,” For we walk by faith, not by sight.”
In 2023, Jeffries was put forward by Democrats as their pick to succeed former US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy, who was ousted by his fellow Republicans in favour of the chamber’s current speaker, Mike Johnson. Wednesday’s vote, however, means Jeffries has now been formally nominated by members of his party.
Jeffries is poised to replace Johnson as speaker when the new Congress is sworn in on January 3 with a Democratic majority and a vote on the new speaker is held in the full chamber.

Kuwait condemned the attack, which Iran said targeted an airbase hosting US forces (file photo)
Kuwait and Bahrain have said they repelled Iranian air attacks overnight as hostilities between Iran and the United States rise.
The drone attack on Kuwait was the first in more than two months. The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase, which hosts US forces, but Kuwaiti authorities did not report any damage.
It came after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials.
Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' state oil firm said a crew member was missing after one of its tankers was attacked in the Gulf waterway on Tuesday.
The recent exchanges of fire, as well as deadlock in negotiations on a peace deal, have raised fears of a major escalation in the nine-month-old war.
The conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Since then, Iran has retaliated for US and Israeli strikes by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.
It has also attacked dozens of commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass.

Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
On Tuesday night, Kuwait's military said its air defences engaged "drone threats" but did not report any casualties or damage.
The Kuwaiti foreign ministry condemned the attack, saying it "flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, directly threatened its security and stability, and constituted a grave breach of international law".
"The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying," Hani Mohammed, an Egyptian resident of Kuwait, told AFP news agency.
Bahrain's military also said on Wednesday that its air defence systems had "intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks".
The island kingdom, which hosts the US Navy's 5th Fleet, has reported four attacks over the past six days, following a two-month lull.
Qatar, which has mediated in the stalled indirect talks between Iran and the US, said the Iranian attacks on its neighbours were a "dangerous escalation that threatens to complicate efforts aimed at containing tensions".
The Iranian army said its drones had targeted US Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait.
Later, the army's commander-in-chief, Maj Gen Amir Hatami, warned the US and its allies that it would respond more forcefully to any new attacks on Iran.
"If the enemy repeats its mistake... we have the readiness and the plans to confront it and its supporters in a stronger, more crushing way and without geographic limitations," he said.
On Tuesday night, US fighter jets targeted a missile launch site on Qeshm Island "with precision munitions" in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets", US military officials said.
Iranian media reported explosions on the island but cited a local official as saying they had caused no damage to infrastructure.
In a separate development, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (Adnoc) said a search-and-rescue operation was under way for a missing sailor following an attack on one of its vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The rest of the crew were safely evacuated and 11 were receiving medical care, it added.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre reported that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles (24km) north of Khasab, in Oman's Musandam peninsula. It said the attack caused a fire on board that was extinguished.
Iran said two oil tankers and a ship carrying liquefied natural gas (LNG) had caught fire after hitting naval mines while sailing along an "authorised route".
At least 25 seafarers have been killed across the Middle East since the start of the war, when the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports.
The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the conflict and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.
Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.
In recent months, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling through the Strait of Hormuz, allowing crude oil exports from Gulf states to reach around 80% of pre-war levels, according to analysts.

Democrat Mary Peltola flipped the US Senate seat in Alaska on Tuesday after a tight race that unseated Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan, according to the official ballot count.
With 50.12% of the vote, Peltola's win means the US Senate will have a 56-44 Democratic majority, clinching the chamber's last open race in a midterm election that crushed Republicans across the country and handed US President Donald Trump a firm rebuke of his second term.
"As our next United States Senator, I will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in DC and deliver results for Alaska's working families," Peltola said in a statement late on Tuesday.
"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honour than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs and put Alaska first."
With far-flung rural voters in remote villages, the vote count in Alaska took two weeks to complete, but offered Peltola a strong mandate.
With 144,302 votes, Peltola beat Sullivan's 131,844 votes, even when combined with a second candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. who earned 4,760 votes.
Trump had called for another Republican candidate in the race, Gerald Heikes, to have his votes "immediately given" to Dan S. Sullivan, calling it the "fair solution."
Heikes won 6,105 votes in the race, but merging all the votes that Trump wanted to combine would still not have been enough to beat Peltola.
The Alaska Senate race had attracted national attention following a New York Times investigation revealing that aides to Peltola had recruited another man named Dan Sullivan to run for office with the goal of siphoning votes from the Republican incumbent.
"My opponent's campaign is literally focused on misleading Alaskans, lying and cheating," Senator Sullivan told reporters in Anchorage on election day.
The fact that there were two candidates named Dan Sullivan had repeatedly drawn the ire of Trump, who said Democrats had used a "decoy" to siphon votes from the Republican candidate.
The Trump administration had gone so far as to ask the courts to block certification of the results if the incumbent Sullivan lost because of the potential mix-up.
The legal bid, which Trump has said he ordered personally, sparked alarm in political circles, but was dismissed by a federal judge ahead of the election.
However, US Attorney Michael Heyman claimed federal investigators were conducting both criminal and civil probes involving the Alaska Senate race.
Peltola's historic victory makes her one of the first two Native American women ever to be elected to the US Senate, where she will join Minnesota Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan.
Democrats will control 56 seats in the 100-seat Senate which will give them the power to block legislation, launch broad investigations into Trump's administration and thwart his judicial and senior government appointments.

Case involving allegations from two women employed at singer’s properties in Caribbean had been shelved
A Spanish court is investigating the singer Julio Iglesias over complaints that he sexually abused and physically assaulted two female employees who worked at his properties in the Caribbean.
The announcement of the investigation by the Audiencia Nacional comes almost 11 months after Spanish prosecutors shelved the women’s complaints , arguing the country’s courts had no jurisdiction as the alleged offences took place outside Spain.
But the human rights NGO Women’s Link Worldwide , which is representing the women, has successfully argued that the Audiencia Nacional has jurisdiction over the case and Iglesias’s Spanish nationality provides sufficient grounds to try the case in Spain. It filed a new criminal complaint on the women’s behalf on 3 September.
The allegations emerged in January this year after a three-year joint investigation by the Spanish news site elDiario.es and the Spanish-language TV network Univision Noticias, which gathered testimony from 15 former employees who worked for the now 83-year-old singer between the late 1990s and 2023.
The two complainants – a domestic worker and a physical therapist who were employed at Iglesias’s mansions in the Dominican Republic and the Bahamas – allege the veteran entertainer subjected them “to inappropriate touching, insults and humiliation … in an atmosphere of control and constant harassment”. The offences are alleged to have occurred in 2021.
In a statement released on Wednesday, the Audiencia Nacional said it was investigating the women’s complaint, which accuses Iglesias of “offences against sexual freedom, as well as offences involving bodily harm and degrading treatment”.
The investigating judge, Antonio Piña, said preliminary evidence offered by one of the complainants was sufficient to launch an investigation.
“A photograph of the complainant shows a bruise on one of her arms, consistent with her having been gripped forcefully,” said Piña. “In the same photograph, two marks are visible on one of her thighs – marks that could correspond to a human bite – which the complaint states are the result of her being forced to participate in sexual acts.”
The judge said the “detailed” account submitted, taken with the preliminary evidence provided, was “sufficient to initiate proceedings, without this implying any evaluative judgment regarding the complainant’s credibility”.
However, Piña rejected the women’s allegations of human trafficking and labour offences, and also noted that some of the alleged offences may have expired under the statute of limitations. The judge has called the two women to give evidence in person on 3 February next year.
Iglesias, who has sold more than 300m records during his six-decade career, has denied all the allegations and said he would defend himself against what he described as “a serious affront”.
In a statement posted on Instagram in January, Iglesias wrote: “With great regret, I am responding to the allegations from two people who used to work in my house. I have never abused, coerced or disrespected any woman. These accusations are absolutely false and pain me deeply.”
Women’s Link said the case showed the need for states to ensure access to justice.
“Everyone has the right to have justice systems investigate facts when there are indications of alleged human rights violations,” said Jovana Ríos Cisneros, the NGO’s executive director. “The Spanish state has an obligation to guarantee equal access to justice, regardless of who the accused person is.”

Iranian attacks on the Gulf countries draw condemnation from across the region.
Iran has launched new attacks on its Gulf neighbours, targeting an airbase used by the United States military in Kuwait and carrying out several attacks on Bahrain after the US bombed Iran’s Qeshm Island.
Kuwait said it activated its air defences to counter drone strikes – the first since early September – and Bahrain said it fended off an Iranian attack early on Wednesday, a day after the US attacked a missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
The US said it carried out the strike in response to an Iranian attack on a US radar installation in Bahrain earlier on Tuesday.
Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy’s 5th Fleet, has experienced four Iranian attacks in six days, ending a weeks-long respite in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.
Iran said its recent attacks were in response to US drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers.
The uptick in fighting raises the risk of a wider escalation towards the resumption of all-out conflict nearly nine months into the war, and complicates negotiations for a diplomatic solution, which have stagnated despite intensified mediation efforts from Qatar.
The Iranian attacks on the Gulf countries have drawn condemnation from across the region.
Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain “in the strongest terms” and denounced an attack on a tanker belonging to the United Arab Emirates.
The ministry said the kingdom rejects Iran’s disruption of shipping routes and urged a negotiated solution.
Arab League chief Nabil Fahmy said the repeated attacks on Arab countries reveal “a continuous escalation pattern that threatens to widen the circle of confrontation”. He also condemned the targeting of a ship belonging to the UAE’s national oil company, ADNOC, as it crossed the Strait of Hormuz.
Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, the Gulf Cooperation Council’s secretary-general, held Iran “responsible for this escalation and its repercussions on regional security”.
Qatar’s Foreign Ministry called the attacks “a dangerous escalation” that risks undermining diplomatic efforts. Kuwait and the UAE also condemned them.
Kuwait’s Foreign Ministry described the drone attacks as flagrant violations of its sovereignty and a direct threat to its security, Al Jazeera’s Zein Basravi reported from Doha.
Basravi also said Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesman, Majed al-Ansari, warned that continued escalation without restraint from both the US and Iran makes a negotiated solution, or even continued dialogue, harder.
Meanwhile, Iran’s army chief, Major-General Amir Hatami, said the armed forces were “monitoring the enemy’s movements” after a third US aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East, the Fars news agency reported.
He said Iran’s response to any misstep by the US and its “backers” would be “even more crushing”.

Singer Julio Iglesias is facing an investigation by Spain's national court over allegations he sexually abused and assaulted two female former staff members
Two women, who worked for the 83-year-old in the Caribbean, have accused him of abuse which they say took place in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic in 2021.
The announcement comes after Spanish prosecutors dropped an inquiry into the claims earlier this year after concluding that they lacked jurisdiction because the alleged crimes took place abroad.
Iglesias, who has been a household name in Spain since the 1960s and has sold millions of records worldwide, has previously denied the allegations .
But in a statement published on Wednesday , external (in Spanish), national court Judge Antonio Piña said the account given in the complaint, alongside preliminary evidence provided, justified opening criminal proceedings.
He added that the investigation would cover parts of the complaint relating to potential crimes against sexual freedom, as well as assault and degrading treatment.
But the court will not investigate claims made in the lawsuit of human trafficking or crimes against workers' rights. Piña said these allegations were dismissed after the he looked into the hiring of the women and found there was "no deception or artifice involved".
Piña said the former employees had been summoned to testify in person on 3 February.
The announcement comes after Spain's public prosecutor's office shifted its position last month, saying it now believed the court had jurisdiction to investigate the allegations.
In its statement, the national court said Spanish law sets out that courts can hear cases of crimes committed abroad by Spanish citizens provided certain conditions are met.
The allegations against Iglesias first emerged in a joint three-year investigation between Spanish newspaper El Diario , external and television network Univision news, published in January.
In that investigation, the two women were identified as a domestic worker and a physical therapist, who described alleged sexual abuse and degrading working conditions.
The domestic worker, whose name was changed to Rebeca in the reports, said Iglesias would regularly call her to his room at the end of the day and would touch her inappropriately without consent.
Rebeca, a Dominican who was 22 when the alleged events took place, also alleged that Iglesias had forced her to take part in threesomes with another female member of staff. She also described the singer slapping her in the face and grabbing her genitals.
The other woman, a Venezuelan physical therapist named as Laura in the article, said Iglesias had touched her breasts and kissed her on the mouth against her will. She added that he constantly threatened to fire her, controlled how much food she ate and asked her about when her period was due.
Rebeca and Laura filed an initial legal complaint in January against Iglesias for sexual assault and human trafficking.
In a response to the allegations in January, Iglesias said , external : "I deny having abused, coerced, or disrespected any woman. These accusations are absolutely false and deeply sadden me."
On Wednesday, the court said the lawsuit had been accepted based on evidence provided in the complaint. This included a photograph of one of the complainants, showing a bruise on her arm that was "consistent with the possibility of her being grabbed forcefully".
It added that the same photo showed "two marks on one of her thighs that could correspond to a human bite", which the complainant said were "a consequence of her forced participation in acts of a sexual nature".
WhatsApp message exchanges, including New Year's greetings, which suggest an "affectionate" relationship between the women and Iglesias, will also be considered, the court said.
But it added that the seemingly cordial tone, which presents "an apparent discrepancy with certain aspects of the narrative", would be clarified through a "complete and contextualised examination of the communications".
The claim over violations of workers' rights could not be investigated because there is no comparable criminal offence in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic, where the alleged crimes took place, it said.
Iglesias is one of the most successful Latin artists of all time, having sold more than 300 million records in a career spanning decades.
He is also the father of fellow music superstar Enrique Iglesias.

Trump, Xi and Putin will hold their first trilateral meeting on the sidelines of APEC. With different priorities on trade, Ukraine, Iran and arms control, what does each leader hope to gain?
The leaders of China , the United States and Russia are due to hold their first trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit this week.
Separately, US President Donald Trump will also hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping during the November 18-19 gathering in Shenzhen, China.
Several experts interviewed by DW do not expect any breakthroughs on US-China trade, technology or other issues. Maintaining the existing trade truce and preventing bilateral relations from deteriorating further may be the more realistic shared objectives.
Patricia M. Kim, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, believes neither leader is looking to significantly expand the bilateral agenda, as both have an incentive in maintaining the existing trade truce.
Over the next two years, Kim expects to see "neither uncontrolled escalation in tensions between the US and China nor a dramatic improvement in ties, but rather the continuation of the transactional détente we see today."
Zhang Lun, a professor at CY Cergy Paris University, believes Trump is under pressure both at home and abroad.
"Domestically, Trump faces the prospect of becoming a lame-duck president following the Republicans' heavy losses in the midterm elections," Zhang told DW.
"Internationally, damage to relations with allies, the weakening of the US-led international order, indifference toward democratic values and freedoms, and the difficulties encountered in the Iran war have all reduced America's leverage, resources and influence."
Zhang believes strained ties with US allies and the war in Iran have weakened Trump's hand with Beijing, making him more eager to secure diplomatic wins and Xi's cooperation on key policy priorities.
Jia Hui Tee, a senior trade policy analyst at the Hinrich Foundation, expects Trump and Xi to focus on stabilizing their fragile trade relationship.
She says the two leaders could make progress on reciprocal tariff cuts covering goods worth $30 billion (€27.3 billion) on each side. "While the list of products has been announced, the timeline has not been set and an indicative implementation timeline would be an easy win" for both governments.
Washington wants Beijing to accelerate purchases of US agricultural products and increase exports of rare earths and other critical minerals. But Tee believes that "China would likely be cautious with delivering on its commitments especially when Trump is weaker at home after the midterms with Democrats pushing back on his tariffs."
She also points out that neither side would want to cede their bargaining chips easily, including rare earth exports and technology export controls.
With another meeting between the two leaders is expected in December at the G20 summit in Miami, "there is room to push more contentious issues to a later date and further extend the trade truce in the next meeting," Jia told DW.
Russia hopes that talks with the leaders of the US and China will enhance its diplomatic standing and help secure a settlement to the war in Ukraine on terms favorable to Moscow.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center, told DW that Moscow wants to create the impression that Washington is willing to sit down with Russia and negotiate. This, in turn, could undermine confidence in Europe and Ukraine .
"Trump wants trilateral nuclear talks," she said, while Beijing "wants the optics of China hosting the unprecedented historical meeting among the three."
Alicja Bachulska, a policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, believes Beijing wants to use the meeting to demonstrate its ability to bring major powers together and facilitate international dialogue.
"Russia wants recognition, the US wants arms control, and China wants status without strings attached," she said. "I expect each leader to restate their own positions rather than produce real solutions."
Michael Kimmage, director of the Kennan Institute in the United States, told DW last month that China may be more concerned with the survival of Russian President Vladimir Putin's regime than with actively bringing the war in Ukraine to an end.
Russia remains an important source of energy and a key diplomatic partner for Beijing, Kimmage noted.
An outright Russian victory may not necessarily be Beijing's objective, he said. "More important to China is the political survival of Vladimir Putin." For that reason, Kimmage does not expect China to pressure the Russian president into ending the war if Putin is unwilling to do so.
Zhang Lun believes the current situation is "most in line with Beijing's interests."
The Trump administration's pro-Putin stance has made it harder for Ukraine to resist Russia, Zhang said, while Europe has been forced to bear greater costs and has been weakened.
He argued that the United States has also "lost moral authority" and "the postwar international order and the alliances built around Washington have been further eroded," making China's "position and influence more prominent."
He believes Beijing wants to keep Russia from collapsing, but not support it so openly or extensively that it alienates Europe and other Western countries.
"At the same time, China does not want Ukraine to be defeated, because that would reduce Russia's dependence on Beijing," he told DW.
"For now, China is unlikely to intervene directly. Instead, it will wait for a more favorable moment and then potentially step in as a neutral mediator in order to maximize its gains."
W.A. Figueroa, an assistant professor of history and international relations at the University of Groningen in the Netherlands, told DW that there is little indication of any real cooperation between China and the US on Iran .
The two countries do share some interests, "including opposition to a toll system in the Strait of Hormuz and opposition to nuclear proliferation," Figueroa noted, but "China has consistently called for negotiations and denounced both sanctions and military force as a way to achieve these or any other objectives."
Figueroa says China does not want further escalation or prolonged instability in the Middle East. However, Beijing has been able to manage the current situation without too much difficulty, leaving it with little pressure to change its position.
"China continues to provide Iran with crucial financial support through its purchases of Iranian oil," Figueroa noted, adding that Beijing's diplomatic support has so far brought no substantial change, largely because China has little leverage over either Iran or the US in the region.

Israeli tanks have advanced towards central Gaza as the military launched what it called a “precise operation” against Hamas, raising fresh tensions over a ceasefire that has been in place since October 2025.
An AFP journalist reported seeing tanks, driven by the Israeli military, position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp, which is located in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza .
The AFP also heard from a security source in Gaza who said there was "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of the camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza "amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday".
The Israeli military confirmed the attack, saying: “The IDF launched a precise operation within the Gaza Strip earlier today west of the Yellow Line... to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip.”
The so-called Yellow Line separates Israeli and Hamas-controlled areas in Gaza since an uneasy ceasefire began in October 2025. The Israeli military says it controls more than 60% of the Palestinian territory.
Confirming that the operation involved military and Israeli Security Agency personnel, the IDF said, “there is Hamas infrastructure in the area in the central Gaza Strip.”
COGAT, the Israeli defence ministry body responsible for civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories, has warned international aid organisations not to move through the affected areas.
It said the operation would take place near the Al-Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps, with traffic also halted along the Salah al-Din road, Gaza's main thoroughfare.
Hamas condemned the operation as a "flagrant violation" of the ceasefire agreement, accusing Israel of failing to honour its commitments.
The Israeli military, meanwhile, said it was responding to apparent violations of the truce by Hamas.
More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began, according to an AFP tally based on figures from Gaza's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose data is considered reliable by the United Nations.
The Israeli military has reported seven soldiers and one civilian contractor killed over the same period.

At least three Palestinians killed as Israeli forces launch strikes near refugee camp.
Israeli forces killed three Palestinians during a new operation in central Gaza on Wednesday, according to hospital officials, in the first broad ground offensive since a “ceasefire” was signed more than a year ago.
Al Jazeera correspondents on the ground reported that Israeli tanks were operating near Salah al-Din Street, east of the Nuseirat refugee camp and north of the Bureij camp.
An Israeli air strike targeted the town of al-Mughraqa, north of Nuseirat, killing one person and wounding several others, an official at al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera.
Reporting from Gaza City, Al Jazeera’s Hind Khoudary said many Palestinians were fleeing areas in central Gaza as the Israeli operation got under way.
“We have been seeing people in eastern parts of Maghazi and Bureij, and people who are close to Salah al-Din starting to evacuate and flee the area due to the fact that there were huge explosions heard, live ammunition, and artillery shelling in that area,” Khoudary said.
“The Israeli forces in their announcement did not issue an evacuation order for people who are living in this area. They just mentioned that there is a military operation that is going to start, they are going to destroy the infrastructure and they are going to start demolishing in this area,” she added.
Earlier on Wednesday, the Israeli army said the operation aimed to “eliminate a threat” to its forces operating in the area of the “Yellow Line”, which demarcates the Israeli-occupied area of Gaza, and was established under the “ceasefire” agreement signed between Israel and Hamas in October 2025.
In a statement, the Israeli military said: “We reserve the freedom to act and manoeuvre whenever necessary to eliminate any immediate threat in the Gaza Strip.”
Hamas condemned the Israeli operation as a “flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement”.
“Forced evacuation orders and the displacement of citizens carried out under the threat of violence and bombardment constitute a war crime and a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law,” the group said in a statement.
“The occupation’s actions are aimed at herding citizens into a narrow strip of the Gaza Strip, further exacerbating the ongoing humanitarian catastrophe,” it added.
Hamas said it holds Israel and the United States responsible for “the repercussions of the military operation and the crimes committed against civilians”.
Before the announcement of the Israeli operation, two Israeli drone attacks on Gaza killed at least two people, hospital officials told Al Jazeera.
Al-Shifa Hospital reported that one person was killed and others were wounded in an attack on the Sheikh Ijlin neighbourhood in southwestern Gaza City.
In a separate attack, Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital reported that one person was killed in Deir el-Balah in central Gaza, where the hospital had earlier reported an injury.
Earlier on Wednesday, Gaza’s Ministry of Health said that hospitals had recorded seven deaths and received 15 wounded people in the previous 24 hours.
Six people were killed by Israel over that period while one died from injuries caused by an earlier attack, the ministry said.

Watch: Jeff Bezos on involvement in casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond
Jeff Bezos has said he was "heavily involved" in casting Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond.
Speaking at an event in California, the Amazon chairman said he was originally "biased against" Pattinson - who starred in many blockbuster films like Batman and the Twilight series - "because he's already so famous".
The role of 007 has typically gone to an actor who is not as well known at the time of casting. But Bezos said in screen tests, "it was so obvious he is James Bond".
This will be the first 007 film in the official series not under the creative control of the Broccoli family, who had overseen the franchise since the first movie in 1962. Amazon purchased MGM, which co-owns the franchise, in 2022.
'Good Bond vibes' - Hollywood locals react to Robert Pattinson cast as new 007
"There was something special about Rob", Bezos said at Semafor Silicon Valley & The World Event on Tuesday.
Pattinson was unveiled as the franchise's seventh James Bond on Monday, taking over from actor Daniel Craig. He will star in the 26th Bond movie, due to be released in 2028.
In a statement, the London-born actor said: "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime."
The next Bond film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, but its title and exact release date have not yet been announced.
The announcement comes after years of intense speculation about who will take over from Craig in one of the most high-profile - and highly scrutinised - roles in entertainment.
Robert Pattinson was unveiled as the franchise's seventh James Bond on Monday
Several other actors, including Josh O'Connor, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden, were reported to be in the frame for the role as screen tests took place in recent weeks.
But Amazon MGM ultimately went with a household name, choosing a more bankable movie star who is widely seen as a safe pair of hands.
"We ran a really tight process and made the final decision on Friday," Bezos said.
There were five finalists who went through "real, old-fashioned screen tests", acting out three different scenes in full costume, with real sets and other actors, he said.
"By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob and his performance," Bezos added. "It was immediately un-debated. Denis [Villeneuve], the director … we all gravitated toward Rob."
The pick comes amid widespread Hollywood cuts and consolidation, with studios struggling to get people into cinemas.
Hollywood insiders have said Pattinson was viewed as a safe pick to bring audiences in, rather than taking a risk on a new actor who could grow with the franchise.
"Maybe he's boring. Maybe Hollywood would be passing up a chance to anoint a badly needed new star. But with so much at stake for everyone involved, that all makes him the obvious pick," Hollywood journalist Matthew Belloni, who predicted the pick, wrote in his newsletter.

In recent years, highly concentrated products containing 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) have emerged online and at smoke shops, liquor stores and gas stations. These products, available as tablets, gummies, tonics and chocolates, contain one of the major psychoactive ingredients in kratom. Others say it helps them feel energized or focused. Users of 7-OH and kratom can show signs of addiction, and unclear product labeling makes it hard to determine the quantities consumed. Over the past decade, the U.S. government has tried to restrict these products, but public opposition has kept them legal. Recently, this situation has started to change .

Türkiye İstatistik Kurumu (TÜİK), temmuz-eylül dönemine ilişkin iş gücü istatistiklerini açıkladı.
Buna göre, Türkiye genelinde 15 ve daha yukarı yaştaki kişilerde mevsim etkisinden arındırılmış işsiz sayısı, bu yılın temmuz-eylül döneminde bir önceki çeyreğe göre 46 bin kişi artarak 2 milyon 870 bin kişi olarak tespit edildi.
Mevsim etkisinden arındırılmış işsizlik oranı ise 0,1 puan artışla yüzde 8,1 seviyesinde hesaplandı.
İşsizlik oranı, söz konusu dönemde geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre 0,3 puan azaldı.
İşsizlik oranı erkeklerde yüzde 6,8, kadınlarda yüzde 10,7 olarak ölçüldü.
15-24 yaş grubunu kapsayan genç nüfusta mevsim etkisinden arındırılmış işsizlik oranı, bu yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde bir önceki çeyreğe göre 0,1 puanlık artışla yüzde 14,1 oldu. Bu yaş grubunda işsizlik oranı erkeklerde yüzde 10,4, kadınlarda yüzde 21,3 olarak tahmin edildi.
TÜİK geçmişe dönük bazı çeyreklik işsizlik verilerinde revizyona da gitti.
Buna göre, çeyrekler itibarıyla mevsim etkilerinden arındırılmış işsizlik oranları şöyle:
Mevsim etkisinden arındırılmış istihdam edilenlerin sayısı, yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde bir önceki çeyreğe kıyasla 62 bin kişi azalarak 32 milyon 434 bin kişi oldu. İstihdam oranı da 0,3 puan düşüşle yüzde 48,3 olarak tespit edildi. Bu oran erkeklerde yüzde 65,7 iken kadınlarda yüzde 31,4 olarak gerçekleşti.
Mevsim etkisinden arındırılmış iş gücü, söz konusu dönemde 17 bin kişi gerileyerek 35 milyon 304 bin kişiye düştü. İş gücüne katılma oranı da 0,2 puanlık azalışla yüzde 52,6'ya geriledi. İş gücüne katılma oranı erkeklerde yüzde 70,5, kadınlarda yüzde 35,1 oldu.
Bu dönemde istihdam edilenlerin sayısı, bir önceki çeyreğe göre tarım sektöründe 58 bin kişi, sanayi sektöründe 133 bin kişi azalırken inşaat sektöründe 9 bin kişi, hizmet sektöründe 120 bin kişi arttı. İstihdam edilenlerin yüzde 13,6'sı tarım, yüzde 19,3'ü sanayi, yüzde 6,8'i inşaat, yüzde 60,3'ü hizmet sektöründe yer aldı.
İstihdam edilenlerden referans döneminde işbaşında olanların, mevsim ve takvim etkilerinden arındırılmış haftalık ortalama fiili çalışma süresi, bu yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde bir önceki çeyreğe göre değişim göstermeyerek 42,3 saat olarak gerçekleşti.
Zamana bağlı eksik istihdam, potansiyel iş gücü ve işsizlerden oluşan atıl iş gücü oranı, üçüncü çeyrekte bir önceki çeyreğe göre 1 puanlık artışla yüzde 30,9 oldu. Zamana bağlı eksik istihdam ve işsizlerin bütünleşik oranı yüzde 20,5 iken işsiz ve potansiyel iş gücünün bütünleşik oranı yüzde 20,2 olarak tahmin edildi.
Türkiye genelinde temmuz-eylül dönemine ilişkin mevsim etkilerinden arındırılmış temel iş gücü göstergeleri şöyle:
Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanı Vedat Işıkhan, NSosyal hesabından Türkiye İstatistik Kurumunun (TÜİK) temmuz-eylül dönemi iş gücü istatistiklerine ilişkin paylaşımda bulundu.
Bu yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde bir önceki çeyreğe göre 0,1 puanlık artış gösteren işsizlik oranının, geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre 0,3 puanlık azalarak yüzde 8,1 olduğunu belirten Işıkhan, şunları kaydetti:
"İstihdam sayımız, bu yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde 32 milyon 434 bin kişi, istihdam oranımız ise yüzde 48,3 olarak gerçekleşti. İş gücümüz aynı dönemde 35 milyon 304 bin kişi, iş gücüne katılma oranı ise yüzde 52,6 olarak gerçekleşti. Çalışma hayatımızı Ulusal İstihdam Stratejimiz ve Ulusal Adil Geçiş Stratejimiz doğrultusunda güçlendirmek için politikalarımızı sürdüreceğiz. Gençlerimiz başta olmak üzere vatandaşlarımızın iş gücü piyasasına erişimlerinin desteklenmesi için adımlarımıza devam edeceğiz."

Scientists tell Commons committee that exposure to colibactin in early life is a potential driver of early onset colorectal cancer
Exposure to a bacterial toxin in early life has emerged as a leading suspect in the rise of bowel cancer amongs those under 50, MPs have heard.
Cases of early onset bowel cancer have doubled in many countries in the past two decades, and while rising obesity and a fall in physical activity are contributors, researchers believe other factors must also be involved.
Dr Karl Smith-Byrne, a senior molecular epidemiologist at the University of Oxford, told the Commons science and technology committee that known risk factors for colorectal cancer, such as obesity, smoking and alcohol, can explain only about half of the cases doctors diagnose.
He said he did not find it “plausible” that the rise in early onset bowel cancer could be entirely explained by risk factors that researchers were already aware of.
Last year scientists identified a toxin called colibactin, produced by some variants of E coli bacteria in the gut, as a potential driver of early onset colorectal cancer. Hallmark mutations caused by the toxin were three times more common in tumours from people under 40 than in those from people over 70.
More work is needed to understand whether colibactin actually drives bowel cancer, but it is a question scientists are now actively pursuing. “That’s probably the leading explanation at the moment,” Smith-Byrne told MPs.
Prof Mike Stratton at the Sanger Institute, who was not at the hearing, has said that colibactin causes mutations in some children but not others, with evidence of mutations appearing as early as infancy. By the age of 10, affected children can have a similar “mutational burden” to a 50-year-old, his work showed.
“If it is causing mutations, it’s causing mutations at a sensitive period earlier in life, and that can give that person’s colon or their rectum a head start on its journey towards being cancerous or developing these tumours,” said Smith-Byrne, who is himself a survivor of early onset rectal cancer.
Some suspect that particular variants of E coli that normally live harmlessly in the gut have evolved in recent decades to produce colibactin. Prof Elio Riboli, a cancer epidemiologist at Imperial College London, told the committee: “This colibactin is essentially found in people born after 1960. Something has happened in the E coli bacteria … There must have been a mutation, and there is a new bacteria.”
Bowel cancer is the third most common cancer in the world, accounting for about one in 10 of all cases. The disease is still far more common in the over-50s, but global figures suggest diagnoses are rising steeply in younger people.
Prof Helen Coleman, a cancer epidemiologist at Queen’s University Belfast, told MPs that colibactin was “the first new clue that we’ve had in quite some time”, but that its potential role in bowel cancer was still under investigation.
“Even though we’re talking about adults that are being diagnosed with cancer between 18 and 49, it’s quite likely to be very early life exposures,” she said. “It could be something you were exposed to in very early childhood, possibly even in the prenatal period, and that makes it very difficult to study.”
Riboli said that while scientists need to uncover the unknown drivers of different cancers, people should minimise risks that are already clear. In the UK and US, drinking and smoking are both falling, but obesity is rising and physical activity is in decline. “The quick win could come from applying what we know,” he said. “We could prevent about 60% of the cancers occurring now, but we are not applying in society what we know.”

The comments were made by Zia Yusuf , who was previously embroiled in a bitter feud with Robert Jenrick before the former Tory minister made the jump to Nigel Farage’s party earlier this year to become its self-styled ‘shadow chancellor’.
“I don’t think the country has time for us to not be candid about these things,” Yusuf told a podcast by the Spectator magazine when asked about the potential role in Reform of former Conservatives who had served in governments which did not bring migration numbers down.
“So if you are in the category of being concerned about [former Conservatives being involved in Reform], none of the above are going to be involved in immigration policy or borders policy,” he said.
“There’s a reason why Nigel’s given me this brief and not them,” he told the Spectator editor and former Conservative minister, Michael Gove.

2026, Türkiye'deki metal müzik dinleyicileri için gerçekten dolu dolu geçti. Yıllardır sahnelerde görmeyi beklediğimiz efsanelerden metal tarihine damga vurmuş gruplara kadar pek çok isim bu yıl Türkiye'ye geldi. Üstelik yalnızca büyük gruplar değil, farklı metal türlerini temsil eden isimler de konser takviminde kendine yer buldu. Biz de bu yılın en dikkat çekici konserlerini bir araya getirdik. 🤘
Nevermore'un yeniden sahnelere dönmesi metal dünyasında başlı başına heyecan yaratırken grubun İstanbul konseri de yılın dikkat çeken buluşmalarından biri oldu. Jeff Loomis ve Van Williams'ın yeniden bir araya geldiği kadroda, vokalleri Türk solist Berzan Önen üstlendi. Özellikle Dead Heart in a Dead World ve This Godless Endeavor albümleriyle büyüyenler için bu konser, Nevermore'u yıllar sonra yeniden canlı dinleme fırsatıydı. Üstelik grubun yeni döneminde bir Türk vokalistle sahneye çıkması da geceyi daha özel kıldı. 🤘
Death denildiğinde Chuck Schuldiner'ın metal müziğe bıraktığı mirası anmadan geçmek mümkün değil. İşte Death to All da bu mirası yaşatmak için bir araya gelen, grubun eski üyelerinden oluşan oldukça özel bir proje. Teknik death metalin en önemli albümlerinden parçaları canlı dinlemek, özellikle Death'in müziğiyle büyüyenler için kaçırılmayacak bir fırsattı. Üstelik bu konser, Death to All'un Türkiye'deki ilk performansı olması bakımından da ayrı bir öneme sahipti.
Listemizin henüz sahneye çıkmamış ama mutlaka yer vermek istediğimiz ismi Fake Majesty! Metalcore'u elektronik altyapılar ve sinematik atmosferlerle birleştiren grup, 12 Aralık'ta Zorlu PSM %100 Studio'da lansman konserini gerçekleştirecek. 'Ease the Pain', 'Yağmur Damlaları' ve 'Rüya' parçalarıyla kendi müzikal dünyasını oluşturmaya başlayan grup, bu konserde yayımladığı şarkıların yanı sıra yeni çalışmalarını da ilk kez canlı seslendirecek. Yani 2026'nın son büyük metal buluşmalarından biri için şimdiden takvimleri işaretlemekte fayda var!
Thrash metalin en büyük isimlerinden Megadeth, 2026'da Türkiye'ye veda turnesi kapsamında geldi. Dave Mustaine önderliğindeki grubun İstanbul konseri, özellikle yıllardır Megadeth dinleyenler için oldukça duygusal bir buluşmaydı. Peace Sells, Rust in Peace ve Countdown to Extinction gibi albümlerden klasiklerin yanı sıra yeni dönem parçalarının da yer aldığı setlist, grubun kariyerine güzel bir yolculuk sundu. Bir de konserin veda turnesi kapsamında gerçekleştiğini düşününce, bu geceyi sıradan bir Megadeth konseri olarak değerlendirmek pek mümkün değil.
Modern metalin en sevilen gruplarından Trivium da bu yıl İstanbul'da sahne alan isimler arasındaydı. Matt Heafy ve arkadaşları, metalcore ile thrash metalin güçlü taraflarını bir araya getiren müzikleriyle yıllardır geniş bir dinleyici kitlesine sahip. Ascendancy ve Shogun gibi albümlerle büyüyenler için grubun parçalarını canlı dinlemek zaten ayrı bir keyif. Teknik gitar soloları, sert davullar ve seyirciyi sürekli hareket halinde tutan sahne enerjisiyle Trivium, haziran ayının öne çıkan konserlerinden birine imza attı.
Metal müziğin alışılmış kalıplarını bir kenara bırakan BABYMETAL, temmuz ayında İstanbul'daydı. Japon grubun J-pop melodilerini metal riffleriyle birleştiren müziği, ilk duyulduğu günden beri metal dünyasında epey tartışma yarattı ama sahne performanslarıyla da kendini kanıtladı. Koreografiler, kostümler, yüksek enerjili şarkılar ve kusursuz sahne prodüksiyonu derken BABYMETAL konserleri gerçekten kendine has bir deneyim sunuyor. Life Park'taki konserde 'Gimme Chocolate!!', 'RATATATA' ve 'Road of Resistance' gibi parçaları canlı dinlemek de gecenin en güzel anlarındandı.
Groove metalin en önemli gruplarından biri olan Pantera, yıllar sonra ilk kez İstanbul'da sahne aldı. Üstelik gecede Cavalera Conspiracy ve Bodysnatcher da vardı; yani konser daha Pantera sahneye çıkmadan oldukça sert bir başlangıç yaptılar. 'Walk', 'Cowboys From Hell' ve 'I'm Broken' gibi klasiklerin binlerce kişi tarafından hep bir ağızdan söylenmesi, 16 bin kişinin katıldığı bu konseri yılın en görkemli metal buluşmalarından birine dönüştürdü.
Heavy ve power metal dünyasının kült gruplarından Savatage, yaklaşık 20 yıla yaklaşan uzun aranın ardından yeniden sahnelere dönmüştü. 2026 yazındaki Avrupa turnesinin duraklarından biri de İstanbul oldu. Üstelik bu konser grubun İstanbul'daki ilk performansıydı. 'Hall of the Mountain King', 'Gutter Ballet' ve 'Sirens' gibi parçalarla metal tarihine adını yazdıran grubu yıllar sonra canlı izlemek, özellikle eski kuşak metal dinleyicileri için oldukça özel bir deneyimdi.
Groove metalin en güçlü temsilcilerinden grup, yıllardır yüksek tempolu performansları ve sert sound'uyla tanınıyor. İstanbul konserinde onlara Orbit Culture ve Türkiye'den Black Tooth da eşlik etti. Randy Blythe'ın sahnedeki enerjisi, Mark Morton ve Willie Adler'ın gitarlarıyla birleşince ortaya tam anlamıyla kafa sallamalık bir gece çıktı. Özellikle 'Laid to Rest', 'Redneck' ve 'Walk with Me in Hell' gibi parçaları canlı dinlemek isteyenler için temmuz ayının kaçırılmaması gereken konserlerinden biriydi.
İsveç'in Göteborg şehrinden çıkan ve melodik death metalin gelişiminde büyük pay sahibi olan In Flames, temmuz ayında İstanbul'da sahne aldı. Grubun özellikle The Jester Race, Whoracle ve Colony dönemindeki işleri, melodik death metal sevenler için hâlâ ayrı bir yerde duruyor. Konserde In Flames'e Napalm Death ve Employed to Serve de eşlik etti. Böylece gece, farklı kuşaklardan ve farklı sertlik seviyelerinden metal gruplarını aynı sahnede buluşturdu.
Tek bir konserle yetinmeyenler için 2026'nın en önemli buluşmalarından biri de Bosphorus Open Air Metal Fest oldu. Beşinci kez düzenlenen festival, iki gün boyunca farklı ülkelerden ve metal türlerinden pek çok grubu aynı sahnede buluşturdu. Satyricon, Moonspell, Kataklysm, Tankard, I Am Morbid, Terrorizer, Kampfar ve Eleine gibi isimlerin yer aldığı kadro, özellikle ekstrem metal dinleyicilerini fazlasıyla mutlu etti. Black metalden death metale, thrash metalden gotik metalin karanlık atmosferine kadar uzanan programıyla festival, 2026'nın en kapsamlı metal etkinliklerinden biri olarak öne çıktı.

Children’s Health Defense was removed from Facebook and Instagram in 2022. Meta declined to comment on why it allowed the group back
An anti-vaccine group led for years by Robert F Kennedy Jr has been allowed back on Facebook and Instagram, four years after Meta removed the group for repeatedly violating its misinformation policies.
A review by the Guardian found that Children’s Health Defense (CHD) has reopened or opened six accounts on Facebook and Instagram from May through September this year. The group is using its accounts to share false and misleading information about topics including vaccines and deadly measles outbreaks at a time when measles has come roaring back. Health officials have reported 10 measles-associated deaths in the United States this year, and the country this week lost its measles elimination status in an official recognition that it is again endemic in the US after being eliminated for 26 years.
The CHD news comes after a Guardian investigation this month found health and vaccine misinformation was rampant on Facebook in a massive public group, Crunchy Moms, and that Facebook was recommending it to users despite apparent violations of its policies. Crunchy Moms was started a few months after Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg last year announced a rollback of moderation and factchecking. Zuckerberg defended the move at the time by saying he wanted to restore “free expression on our platforms”.
Kennedy now serves as the US health secretary, and CHD continues to have close ties to him. He headlined their annual conference in September.
The group was removed from both Facebook and Instagram by Meta in 2022, after years of criticism that Kennedy and his group were top spreaders of false information about vaccines, Covid-19 and other topics on the platforms. Meta said at the time it “ removed these accounts for repeatedly violating our policies ”, and told CHD it was because its accounts went against community standards on “misinformation that could cause physical harm”.
In 2023, Meta restored Kennedy’s Instagram account, which he had lost in 2021 for sharing false information about Covid and vaccines. The company said it made the decision because Kennedy was an active candidate for US president. But it also said it would not restore CHD’s accounts .
Meta declined to comment on why it allowed CHD back on its platforms and why it was allowing apparent violations of its misinformation policy by CHD.
Kennedy frequently tussled with Facebook before he entered the government. CHD sued Facebook in 2020, when Kennedy was leading the group, claiming it was being censored. The case was dismissed the following year, with the judge finding that Facebook, as a private entity, could not be held liable for violating the group’s constitutional rights. Earlier this year, the Washington Sun reported that Meta’s lawyer argued in a lawsuit in New Mexico that the judge should consider Kennedy’s trustworthiness and “unusual” views on vaccines when urging it not to enter a government-produced report into evidence in a lawsuit over the company’s child safety practices.
Dorit Reiss, a professor at UC Law San Francisco who has closely monitored CHD’s legal cases, said she did not believe there was a legal reason that Meta would be compelled to put CHD back on its platforms, and that it was possible Meta had simply made a political calculation and ceased to enforce its own anti-misinformation policies.
“Facebook has the right to decide what to do here,” Reiss said. “Meta decided it’s more profitable … that it’s more in their interest to let the misinformers back up.”
The Guardian found several posts on the reinstated and new CHD accounts that appear to violate Meta’s harmful health misinformation policy .
A video posted recently by one of its Facebook accounts is titled: “Vaccines: Your child could die,” and makes the misleading claim that vaccines are deadly. Another one earlier this month said: “Somehow there’s this narrative, vaccines are safe and effective, and we know that’s just a lie.”
A video posted last month to at least two of its accounts says of the six measles-associated deaths reported in Pennsylvania at that time: “None of them died from the measles.” Another said the MMR vaccine is “not so safe and effective”. Another said none of the vaccines ever eliminated any epidemic in history.
Another post this month suggested it was unsafe to follow doctors’ recommendations to get multiple vaccinations at once. A June 2026 video posted by the account says the HPV vaccines are “very dangerous”, have “caused hundreds, thousands of deaths” and do not prevent cervical cancer.

Ekim ayında yamalanan PHP güvenlik açıklarının ortaya çıkarılmasında rol oynayan ABD merkezli siber güvenlik şirketi Calif, yapay zeka kullanarak yeni bir kritik güvenlik açığı keşfetti. Bu kez açık, dünyada en yaygın kullanılan Java çalışma ortamı OpenJDK'de tespit edildi.
ABD merkezli girişim Calif, salı günü yaptığı açıklamada Java'nın bellek işlevlerinde bir hata keşfettiğini duyurdu. Söz konusu açık, saldırganların herhangi bir parola veya oturum açma bilgisine ihtiyaç duymadan, internet üzerinden savunmasız bir bilgisayar sunucusunun kontrolünü tamamen ele geçirmesine olanak tanıyabilir.
Java, dünyanın en popüler üçüncü programlama dili konumunda ve Fortune 500 listesindeki şirketlerin yüzde 90'ı tarafından kullanılıyor.
Bankacılık ve finans hizmetlerinden bulut bilişim ve büyük veri altyapılarına, havacılık, telekomünikasyon ve sağlık gibi kritik sektörlerden akıllı telefonlara ve internete bağlı çeşitli cihazlara kadar geniş bir kullanım alanına sahip.
Python, Go ve Kotlin gibi daha yeni programlama dilleri, veri bilimi ve mobil uygulamalar gibi alanlarda pazar paylarını artırmış olsa da Java, küresel kurumsal bilişim altyapısının temel taşlarından biri olmayı sürdürüyor.
Calif, keşfini kamuoyuna duyurmadan önce, savunma tarafındaki kuruluşların siber suçlulardan önce güvenlik yamalarını hazırlayabilmesi için Beş Göz (Five Eyes) istihbarat ittifakının üyeleri olan ABD, Kanada, Birleşik Krallık, Avustralya ve Yeni Zelanda'nın yanı sıra büyük bulut hizmeti sağlayıcılarıyla koordinasyon sağladı.
Avrupa'da ise ulusal siber güvenlik kurumları, Java'nın küresel ölçekte bakımına öncülük eden Oracle ve diğer açık kaynak yazılım geliştiricileri tarafından yayımlanan güvenlik yamalarının uygulanmasını takip etmek üzere acil müdahale ekipleriyle koordinasyon yürütüyor.
Calif tarafından Java4Shell olarak adlandırılan güvenlik açığı, OpenJDK'nin Base64 kod çözücüsünde bulunan bir bellek bozulması (memory corruption) zafiyeti olarak tanımlanıyor.
OpenJDK, internet dünyasında en yaygın kullanılan çalışma ortamlarından biri. Bu tür yazılım ortamları, kullanıcıların kod çalıştırmasına ve programları yürütmesine olanak tanıyor.
Base64 kod çözücüsü ise kimlik doğrulama protokollerinde, dosya yükleme işlemlerinin kodlanmasında ve ağ mesajlarının iletilmesinde kullanılıyor. Calif'e göre bu mekanizma, ikili verilerin metin biçiminde temsil edilmesini sağlıyor.
Güvenlik açığı, OpenJDK'nin Base64 kod çözme işlemlerini hızlandırmak için kullandığı bir mekanizmada tespit edildi.
Bu mekanizma, aynı anda çok sayıda baytı işlemek amacıyla x86-64 işlemci komutları olarak bilinen özel talimatlardan yararlanıyor.
Calif, Base64 kod çözme işlemlerini hızlandırmak için optimize edilen bu mekanizmanın saldırılara açık olduğunu belirledi.
Şirkete göre saldırganlar, özel olarak hazırlanmış bozuk veriler göndererek bellekteki bilgilerin üzerine yazabiliyor ve Java'yı, saldırganın yönetici yetkilerine sahip olduğuna inandırabiliyor.
Bu düzeyde erişim elde eden bilgisayar korsanları, kendi kötü amaçlı yazılımlarını çalıştırabiliyor ve şirketin bilişim teknolojileri mühendisleriyle aynı yetkileri kullanabiliyor.
Bu durum, hassas verileri tehlikeye atarken saldırganlara Java kullanan savunmasız platform ve hizmetlerin kontrolünü ele geçirme imkânı da sağlayabiliyor.

Heavy metal tarihinin en büyük ve en etkili gruplarından Judas Priest , 17 Temmuz 2027'de İstanbul’da müzikseverlerle buluşmaya hazırlanıyor. Metal müziğin gelişimine yön veren, kendine özgü sound’u ve sahne enerjisiyle kuşaklar boyunca müzisyenlere ve dinleyicilere ilham veren efsane grup Judas Priest, İstanbul'a geliyor. Grup Epifoni ve URU ortak organizasyonuyla 17 Temmuz 2027'de KüçükÇiftlik Park sahnesinde olacak.
1969 yılında İngiltere’nin Birmingham kentinde kurulan Judas Priest, yarım asrı aşan kariyeri boyunca heavy metalin yalnızca müzikal sınırlarını değil, sahne kültürünü ve görsel kimliğini de şekillendiren grupların başında geliyor. Rob Halford’un benzersiz vokali, güçlü gitar riffleri ve grubun karakteristik çift gitar sound’u, Judas Priest’i metal tarihinin en belirleyici isimlerinden biri haline getirdi.
“Breaking the Law”, “Living After Midnight”, “You’ve Got Another Thing Comin’”, “Painkiller” ve “Electric Eye” gibi kuşaklar boyunca hafızalara kazınan şarkılara imza atan grup; British Steel, Screaming for Vengeance, Defenders of the Faith ve Painkiller gibi klasik albümleriyle heavy metalin kilometre taşlarını oluşturdu. 50 milyonu aşan albüm satışı ve 2022 yılında Rock & Roll Hall of Fame’e kabul edilmesi de grubun müzik tarihindeki ayrıcalıklı yerini tescilledi.
Siyah deri ve metal aksesuarlarla özdeşleşen ikonik tarzı, sahnedeki güçlü duruşu ve zamana meydan okuyan şarkılarıyla Judas Priest, bugün de heavy metalin en önemli temsilcilerinden biri olmayı sürdürüyor.

Von der Leyen says she wants to give Kyiv ‘strong hand’ in talks and is confident all 27 member states will back idea
The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues.
Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen , said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.”
She expressed confidence all 27 member states would stand behind the loan, despite four central and eastern European countries having already ruled themselves out.
The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said he hoped for the swift adoption of the loan and was counting on the support of all EU member states: “Strong support for Ukraine is the best signal to Russia that this war must end,” he wrote on X.
Zelenskyy convinced EU leaders last month that his country faced a €70bn funding gap in 2027 . The EU pledged to cover €45bn and wants Ukraine’s other allies to cover the rest.
Only 11 months ago, the EU agreed a €90bn loan for Ukraine, which was intended to cover two-thirds of Kyiv’s military and civilian needs in 2026 and 2027. But as Russia’s attacks have escalated , the cost of Ukraine’s defence and the toll of economic disruption continue to rise.
Andrius Kubilius, the EU defence commissioner, said Ukraine’s military spending was increasingly dominated by drones. Ukraine, he told reporters, expected Russia to use 10m drones this year and 20m in 2027. “Ukraine with EU assistance needs to match – and will match,” he said.
The EU loan is split into two parts: €25bn for weapons and €20bn for civilian needs, including funding essential services, such as schools and hospitals.
Von der Leyen expressed confidence that all member states would support the loan because “all 27 member states say very clearly that they want to support Ukraine”. She said member states could choose to support Ukraine’s civilian needs, rather than military spending.
Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria, however, have said they do not intend to take part in the latest funding round for Ukraine, prompting a warning from the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, that he would block the EU’s seven-year budget unless all countries got onboard.
The four central and eastern countries are net beneficiaries of the EU budget, while Germany is the largest payer and Ukraine’s biggest EU donor.
The EU wants Ukraine’s non-EU allies – such as Norway, the UK and Canada – to find €25bn for Kyiv in 2027.
The EU proposal included provisions “to help other countries to help us”, a senior commission official said. Brussels has proposed that G7 countries that provide new loans get guarantees that the borrowing can be repaid with future profits from Russia’s frozen assets.
The profits from the Russian assets are being used to repay a €45bn loan issued by the G7 to Ukraine in 2024.
Countries with a triple-A credit rating could opt to provide guarantees to the EU budget up to €5bn to expand European borrowing for Ukraine on capital markets. The commission has identified six countries that fall into this category: Australia, Canada, Liechtenstein, Norway, Singapore and Switzerland.
EU officials previously said the UK and other allies needed to do more to support Ukraine in 2027, arguing that the EU was shouldering too much of the burden. The UK subsequently pledged a £10bn economic and military support package for Ukraine.
Zelenskyy said: “The UK, Canada, Japan, and Norway have been helping tremendously in our defence of life, and establishing clear rules under which they can provide further aid in conjunction with the EU will help even more.”

İlişkilerini uzun süre gözlerden uzak yaşamayı tercih eden ikili, zaman zaman tatillerden ve davetlerden gelen görüntülerle gündeme geliyor. Çift bu kez Etiler'de akşam yemeğinin ardından objektiflere yansıdı ve gazetecilerin sorularını yanıtladı.
Çağatay Ulusoy ile Aslıhan Malbora, Netflix dizisi Kübra'da başrolü paylaşmıştı. Dizinin setinde kurulan arkadaşlık zamanla yakınlaşmaya, ardından da aşka dönüştü.
Ulusoy'un Malbora'dan önce yaklaşık yedi yıl süren bir ilişkisi vardı. Malbora ile birlikteliği ise önce arkadaşlık olarak başlayan, sonra magazin gündemine oturan bir ilişkiye dönüştü.
İlişkileri, haberlere göre Aralık 2024'te ikilinin İstanbul Havalimanı'nda el ele görüntülenmesiyle kamuoyuna yansıdı. Çift, özel hayatları hakkında çok konuşmasa da sık sık tatil görüntüleriyle ve birlikte katıldıkları davetlerle gündeme geldi. Aralık 2024'te yılbaşını Paris'te karşılayacakları da basına yansımıştı.
Bu yıl Itır Esen ile Engin Aykanat'ın İstanbul'daki düğününde de birlikte yer aldılar. Gecede sahne alan Serdar Ortaç, Malbora'yı sahneye davet edip arkasındaki Ulusoy'u göstererek 'Bununla evlenecek misin?' diye sormuş, Malbora bu soru karşısında utanmıştı. Ulusoy ise olanları gülümseyerek izlemişti.
Malbora'nın Şubat 2026'da sosyal medyada paylaştığı bir karenin ilişkilerini açıkça duyurduğu da aktarılmıştı. Çiftin evlilik planlarına dair bir açıklaması ise bulunmuyor.
Çağatay Ulusoy ile Aslıhan Malbora, Etiler'de bir mekandan çıkarken görüntülendi. İkili akşam yemeğinin ardından gazetecilerin sorularını yanıtladı. Ulusoy, sevgilisi Malbora ile otomobiline binerek mekandan ayrıldı. Haberde mekanın adı belirtilmiyor.
Gazetecilerin sorularını yanıtlayan Ulusoy, kuzeninin ziyareti nedeniyle bir araya geldiklerini ve birlikte yemek yediklerini söyledi. Son dönemdeki kilolarıyla ilgili zayıflama sırrı sorulan oyuncu, yalnızca diyet yaptığını belirtti. Sete ara verdiği dönemlerde neler yaptığı sorulduğunda ise 'Genelde dinlenmeye çalışıyorum' yanıtını verdi.
